column1: # Telex tone keys, spec §3.2 and §3.4. New tone style (the file name carries no
# style suffix), so `oa`, `oe` and `uy` mark their first vowel: `hóa`, not `hoá`.
# Every tone key on every vowel spelling the table can hold: twelve vowels times
# five tones. A reading of the table, not a word list, so it is the same source as
# `unicode.rs`; the expected values are Vietnamese orthography.
# s = sắc (acute), f = huyền (grave), r = hỏi (hook above), x = ngã (tilde),
# §3.4 rule 1: a quality diacritic takes the tone wherever it sits in the syllable.
# §3.4 rule 2: a closed syllable marks its last nucleus vowel, whatever the style.
# §3.4 rule 3: an open syllable marks the first of two vowels, the middle of three.
# `oa`, `oe` and `uy` move under the new style only; every other open pair does not.
# `qu` and `gi` are onsets, so the tone lands on the vowel after them.
# A later tone key replaces the tone instead of adding a second one.
# Doubling a tone key undoes it and keeps the letter; `z` removes the tone and puts
# the tone key's letter back where it was typed.
# A tone key typed before the coda is accepted and the mark moves when the coda
# arrives: this is `free_tone_mark`, which is on by default.
# Case follows the vowel that carries the mark.
# Words end at whitespace, so a tone cannot leak into the next word.
